facts.raw_span: a woman in her 60s presented with an itchy plaque on the mid-back
had had a lesion at that site since childhood, which had remained asymptomatic and pea sized for most of that time
over the 10 years prior to presentation it had gradually increased in size and became itchy
occasional oozing of serosanguineous fluid and bleeding from the lesion
1.5 × 1.0-cm well-defined erythematous plaque with overlying ulceration on the mid-back, 1 cm left of the spine
adjoining skin showed a horseshoe-shaped oval area of lichenification
circumscribed tumor contiguous with adjoining normal epidermis and delineated from underlying dermis by continuous apocrine epithelial lining
tumor epithelium with multiple papillary projections with vascular, plasma cell–rich stroma
several foci showed papillary projections lined by multilayered epithelium with atypical cells, few mitotic figures, and areas of necrosis but no dermal invasion
p63 staining positive in myoepithelial cell layers
adjacent skin showed dermal papillae with congophilic amorphous eosinophilic deposits
pan-cytokeratin (AE1/3) immunostain positive

concepts.why: The presence of a circumscribed tumor with apocrine epithelial lining, papillary projections, and positive p63 staining in myoepithelial cell layers supports this diagnosis.
The tumor's apocrine epithelial lining and positive p63 staining suggest an apocrine gland origin.
The presence of papillary projections with vascular, plasma cell-rich stroma and dermal papillae with congophilic deposits supports this diagnosis.

rationales.F07: The presence of a circumscribed tumor with an apocrine epithelial lining is highly suggestive of Hidradenoma Papilliferum.
rationales.F08: The tumor epithelium with multiple papillary projections and vascular, plasma cell-rich stroma is consistent with Hidradenoma Papilliferum.
rationales.F09: The presence of atypical cells, mitotic figures, and areas of necrosis without dermal invasion is more typical of Hidradenoma Papilliferum than other apocrine gland tumors.
rationales.F10: The positive p63 staining in myoepithelial cell layers supports the diagnosis of Hidradenoma Papilliferum.
rationales.F12: The positive pan-cytokeratin immunostain is consistent with Hidradenoma Papilliferum, but not specific enough to rule out other apocrine gland tumors.

frontier_selector.rationale: The histopathological examination revealed a circumscribed tumor with multiple papillary projections and a continuous apocrine epithelial lining, which is consistent with Hidradenoma Papilliferum. The presence of atypical cells, mitotic figures, and areas of necrosis without dermal invasion also supports this diagnosis.
